objective: Al terminar escribes un relato de una experiencia personal (entrada de blog o artículo) con descripción, sentimientos, narración y reflexión final.

warmup.prompt_es: Escribir sobre una experiencia combina narrar, describir y reflexionar. Aprendes a elegir adjetivos vividos, a expresar emociones con matices y a cerrar con una lección o conclusión personal.

text: Last summer, I did something I had always been afraid of: I travelled alone. I spent ten days in Portugal with nothing but a backpack and a vague plan.

The first day was nerve-racking. I got lost three times in Lisbon's narrow, winding streets, and my phone battery died just when I needed it most. Still, there was something exhilarating about not knowing what would happen next. I ended up in a tiny café where an elderly man taught me how to order coffee in Portuguese. We couldn't understand each other's languages, yet we laughed for an hour.

Over the following days, I climbed up to castles, wandered through markets and watched sunsets from rooftop bars. The sea was a deep, glittering blue, and the smell of grilled sardines drifted through every street. I felt free for the first time in years.
Of course, it wasn't all perfect. One night I felt painfully lonely, and I missed my family. But looking back, those moments taught me as much as the happy ones.
What I learned is that fear usually shrinks when you face it. Would I do it again? Without a doubt. In fact, I'm already planning my next trip.
input.es: Mi primer viaje en solitario. El verano pasado hice algo que siempre me había dado miedo: viajar sola. Pasé diez días en Portugal con una mochila y un plan vago. El primer día fue angustiante. Me perdí tres veces por las estrechas y sinuosas calles de Lisboa, y la batería del móvil se agotó justo cuando más la necesitaba. Aun así, había algo emocionante en no saber qué pasaría a continuación. Acabé en un pequeño café donde un anciano me enseñó a pedir café en portugués. No entendíamos nuestros idiomas, pero nos reímos durante una hora. En los días siguientes subí a castillos, paseé por mercados y vi atardeceres desde bares en azoteas. El mar era de un azul profundo y brillante, y el olor a sardinas a la parrilla flotaba por todas las calles. Me sentí libre por primera vez en años. Por supuesto, no todo fue perfecto. Una noche me sentí dolorosamente sola y eché de menos a mi familia. Pero, mirando atrás, esos momentos me enseñaron tanto como los felices. Lo que aprendí es que el miedo suele encogerse cuando lo afrontas. ¿Lo repetiría? Sin duda. De hecho, ya estoy planeando mi próximo viaje.

md_es: **Estructura de un relato de experiencia**
| Parte | Contenido | Frases útiles |
| **Introducción** | situar y captar interés | *Last summer, I did something I had always been afraid of…* |
| **Desarrollo 1** | primer momento, emociones | *The first day was nerve-racking. · I felt …* |
| **Desarrollo 2** | detalles sensoriales | *The sea was… The smell of… drifted through…* |
| **Contraste** | dificultades | *Of course, it wasn't all perfect. · However, …* |
| **Reflexión** | lo aprendido | *What I learned is that… · Looking back, … · It taught me that…* |
| **Cierre** | opinión final o futuro | *Would I do it again? Without a doubt.* |
**Describir con los sentidos**
- Vista: *glittering, winding, deep blue, golden, towering.*
- Oído: *distant, deafening, murmuring, silent.*
- Olfato: *the smell of…, aroma, fragrance, stench.*
- Gusto: *spicy, rich, bitter, mouth-watering.*
- Tacto: *rough, smooth, freezing, warm.*
**Emociones con matices**
- *Nervous → nerve-racking · happy → delighted, thrilled · sad → heartbroken · tired → exhausted, drained · afraid → terrified.*
- *I felt a mixture of excitement and fear. · I was overcome with joy.*
**Adjetivos -ing y -ed**
- *-ing* describe lo que produce el efecto: *an exhilarating experience.*
- *-ed* describe cómo se siente la persona: *I was exhilarated.*
- ✘ *I was very exciting.* → ✔ *I was very excited.*
**Reflexión final**
- *The experience taught me that… · If I could go back, I would… · I'll never forget… · Looking back, I realise that…*
**Errores típicos**
- ✘ *The trip was very tiring and I felt very excited* (mezcla) → ✔ *The trip was tiring, but I felt excited.*
- ✘ *I was boring.* → ✔ *I was bored.* (cómo me sentí) / *I was boring.* (cómo soy)
- ✘ *In the summer last year…* → ✔ *Last summer…*
- ✘ *I have been in Lisbon the last year.* → ✔ *I went to Lisbon last year.*
- ✘ *The people was friendly.* → ✔ *The people were friendly.*
**Ojo:** *Experience* contable (*an experience*) = vivencia; incontable (*experience*) = práctica. *People* es plural. Evita repetir *nice* y *good*: usa *delightful, memorable, remarkable*.
Pronunciación: *exhilarating* /ɪɡˈzɪləreɪtɪŋ/ · *glittering* /ˈɡlɪtərɪŋ/ · *wander* /ˈwɒndə/ · *nerve-racking* /ˈnɜːv ˌrækɪŋ/.

exercises.prompt: Escribe una entrada de blog (10 a 12 frases) sobre una experiencia memorable (un viaje, una aventura, un reto). Incluye una introducción que capte interés, detalles sensoriales, un momento difícil, adjetivos -ed/-ing y una reflexión final con 'What I learned is that…'.
exercises.model_answer: Last winter, I did something I had never imagined: I spent a weekend in a mountain refuge without electricity. The first evening was nerve-racking, because the temperature dropped below zero and the wind was howling. However, there was something exhilarating about sitting around the fire and playing cards by candlelight. The smell of woodsmoke filled the tiny room, and the stars outside were breathtaking. Of course, it wasn't all perfect. On the second morning I woke up freezing, and I missed my warm bed. Looking back, though, those uncomfortable moments made the experience unforgettable. What I learned is that comfort is not always what makes us happy. Would I do it again? Without a doubt.
